title: Hof backup evidence
description: Written atomically once a backup operation reaches its own end, never touching current.json or the generation (ADR 0006's own Backup Flow step 12) - immutable once written. status distinguishes a real, useful middle case journal/operation-lock-v2 cannot: "partial" (at least one destination succeeded, at least one did not) is recorded honestly here even though the operation's own journal status is always "failed" whenever any configured destination failed - all destinations are required for the operation's own overall success (ADR 0006), but a partial result is never silently reported as a total one.

planId.description: The backup-plan-v1 planId this evidence resulted from - binds this evidence to the exact approved plan, not merely to the backupId it produced.

backupPolicyId.description: The backup-policy-v1 policyId the bound plan itself was built against.

manifestDigest.description: sha256 of the backup-manifest-v1 document actually written into every destination's own snapshot this run - lets a later audit confirm the evidence and the manifest agree on which run this was, without re-opening a snapshot.

backupToolLockDigest.description: The signed backup-tool-lock this operation actually ran under.

status.description: succeeded: every configured destination succeeded. partial: at least one succeeded and at least one failed. failed: no destination succeeded at all (including the case where the operation crashed before any snapshot.create ever ran, leaving perDestinationResults empty).

readinessConfirmedAt.description: When the finally block's own readiness.wait last confirmed the fully-restarted platform ready, after every snapshot/retention attempt - null if the finally block never reached it (a crash inside the finally block itself, not merely a snapshot failure). Without this, evidence could claim status: succeeded (every destination snapshotted) while service.start/readiness.wait/maintenance.exit themselves silently failed to actually restore the platform to a healthy running state - every snapshot succeeding is not the same claim as the platform being left healthy.

allOf.description: status: succeeded requires the finally block to have genuinely completed, not merely every snapshot to have succeeded - a broken restart/readiness/maintenance-exit must never hide behind a claimed backup success.

status must faithfully reflect perDestinationResults' own real content - never a silent partial-as-success or partial-as-total-failure. succeeded additionally requires at least one real result - an empty array is never a success, only ever the crashed-before-any-snapshot.create shape failed alone represents.

retentionApplied.description: Whether retention.apply actually ran to completion for THIS destination's own restic repository - retention is a per-destination operation (a local repo and an S3 repo have entirely independent retention state), never a single run-wide flag. Only ever present on a succeeded destination result; false is never recorded here - a destination that snapshotted successfully but never reached its own retention.apply is still status: succeeded (all-configured-destinations-succeeded is about the snapshot itself, per ADR 0006), simply with retentionApplied absent.

error.description: A short, sanitized diagnostic - never a raw exception dump, a secret value, or credential content.
